title: Pool Helix Throttle Gauge — compact burst & autoscale control prototype
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Design a compact, operator-focused control and health surface for Dedicated GPU pools that surfaces a single-line 'Helix Throttle Gauge' combining thermal, utilization, and burst headroom into an actionable control. The prototype should let operators: 1) view pooled health at a glance, 2) tune autoscale hysteresis and burst headroom (quick presets + advanced modal), 3) preview cost impact and worst-case latency changes, and 4) stage canary rollouts for new autoscale rules. Personas: Platform SRE, Customer Success operator, and internal product managers. Constraints: fits in a left-rail microcard and a full-screen inspector modal; accessible color palettes; should not require new backend fields beyond current telemetry + burst config API. Acceptance criteria: - Readable at 320px width microcard and 1280px inspector. - PM/Eng review signoff on the trade-offs for predictive vs reactive autoscale presets. - Prototype includes a simulated cost delta toggle and a latency percentile preview.

decisions: Use a hybrid radial+sparkline visualization: radial shows current helix score (0-100) and sparkline shows 1h trend. Chosen for scan speed and trend context.

Expose three quick-presets (Conserve / Balanced / Aggressive) and an 'Advanced' inspector for curve tuning. Trade-off: fewer quick-presets reduces config complexity but limits fine-grain control; decided quick-presets win for most operators.
Client-side fallback for missing backend fields to avoid blocking iteration; accurate production mode requires ENG-43112 telemetry fields.
Include cost-preview and latency-percentile simulation in the inspector but not in the compact card to keep the microcard uncluttered.
